rv.q: Lost in Del Valle stands as a testament to the capacities of solo theatre at its most exacting.
Chaos has never been more seductive.
Van Zandt’s playwriting just isn’t taut or dramatic enough to elicit as much appreciation for the storytelling as for the storyteller.
I urge anyone who reads this to buy a ticket and experience live theatre at its most seductive.
This U.S. premiere is as unflinching as it is mesmerizing—an unforgettable descent into the chaos of a life lived on the edge.
That revelation is one of many reasons to see Lost in Del Valle.
His acting talent and skill draw us into this occasionally fragmented, often hilarious, and brutally honest account.

cn.t: Van Zandt's autobiographical solo show about his heroin addiction and prison time divides critics—some praise his theatrical voice and characterization skills, while others find the crudely comic tone and storytelling fall flat.
